clue.text: Novelist and daughter joining the riff-raff

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a disorderly crowd of common people

explanation.surface: A writer's daughter falls in with a low crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret DRABBLE is an English novelist, author of The Millstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is a well-known English writer of fiction, so she is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Pop art's origin seen in this?

definitions.text: Pop art's origin seen in this?

blocks.note: surface reading: the art movement whose anti-art spirit Pop Art grew out of
setter's reading: pop is a word for father, and the answer is two childish words for father put together

explanation.walkthrough: DADA was the early-20th-century anti-art movement that prefigured Pop Art; and pop = DA, so 'Pop' appears in DA-DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism, with Duchamp's readymades, is often cited as a forerunner of the Pop Art movement.

clue.text: A perfect society only half in evidence on account of the car

indicators.note: if only half of something can be seen, the rest of the word has been cut away

blocks.note: taken as written
an imagined ideal world, after Thomas More's book

explanation.surface: An ideal society only partly visible because of motor traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three of the six letters of UTOPIA are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a short informal word for an automobile, that is a motor car.

clue.text: Left-winger with energy and power achieves prominence in Scotland

blocks.note: Tony Benn, the veteran left-wing Labour politician
E is the physics symbol for energy
vis is Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: An energetic, powerful socialist politician becomes famous north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prominence' sounds like fame, but here it means a peak: BEN NEVIS is the highest mountain in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominence is a projecting landform, and Ben Nevis is Scotland's and Britain's tallest mountain.

clue.text: Middle of Fleet Street has work in bar

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the central letter of the five-letter word
St is the abbreviation for street
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Fleet Street, the old home of London newspapers, has a job going in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet Street' reads as one place but splits: the middle letter of Fleet, then the abbreviation for Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to preclude or prevent someone from asserting something, so to bar them.

clue.text: Become enthusiastic, fighting politician outside university

indicators.note: one thing standing outside another wraps around it, so the following letter goes inside

blocks.note: fighting between nations
Member of Parliament
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A warlike politician wrapped around a university, getting fired up.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician's two letters go around the university letter, and the war comes first: WAR + M(U)P gives WARM UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm up to something is to grow keener and more eager about it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Former dictator presented with gold key

blocks.note: Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator of the 1970s
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An ex-tyrant receiving a golden key, perhaps to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the key to a city; the key is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a musical key, the relative minor of C major with no sharps or flats.

clue.text: Sort of boom coming from man with wind

blocks.note: a man's name
a strong wind

explanation.surface: A loud noise produced by a man with flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom' suggests a loud noise, but it is a spar on a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale boom is a short spar under a ship's bowsprit, also called a dolphin striker, which steadies the rigging.

clue.text: A place that offers good mountain views in bad conditions?

definitions.text: A place that offers good mountain views

blocks.clueFragment: A place that offers good mountain views
blocks.note: first meaning taken literally: an attractive route through the mountains
second meaning: the idiom for a sorry state of affairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Things have come to a pretty pass' is the ironic idiom for a bad situation, while literally a pretty mountain pass is a scenic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a gap through mountains, scenic if pretty; idiomatically, a pretty pass is an awkward or unhappy predicament.

clue.text: Blast school when there's a girlfriend around!

indicators.note: the girlfriend is placed around the school, enclosing it

blocks.note: Eton College, the famous English public school
a date is the person you are going out with

explanation.surface: A curse at school life when a girlfriend turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like an exclamation of annoyance but is a verb meaning explode. Eton is the famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast something with explosives is to set off a charge, which is to detonate it.

clue.text: Punch appears in seaside location next to church

blocks.note: a pier is a structure jutting out at a seaside resort
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Mr Punch, of Punch and Judy, performing on a seaside pier beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy puppet shows are traditional at British seaside resorts, which steers you to the puppet, but 'Punch' here is a verb meaning to make a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To punch a hole through something is to perforate it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Serving of veg that is providing iron

blocks.note: mash is mashed potato
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A helping of vegetables supplying iron in the diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like the dietary mineral, but it is a golf club: a mashie is an old name for a five-iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie is an old-fashioned golf club, roughly equivalent to a modern five-iron, so a kind of iron.

clue.text: Philosopher on toilet naps, drifting off

indicators.note: things drifting off wander from their places, so the letters are moved out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker dozing off while seated in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drifting off' fits the dozing picture but tells you the letters wander out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neoplatonist follows the school of thought of Plotinus, built on Plato's ideas, so is a kind of philosopher.

clue.text: It might be tricky for basic actor

indicators.note: something tricky is full of tricks and twists, so the letters are juggled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A part that would be hard for an unsophisticated performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' works twice: acrobatics are full of tricks, and the word tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatics are gymnastic feats and stunts, literally tricks, so they might well be called tricky.

clue.text: Well done, like healthy food

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of congratulation
second meaning: beneficial to one's health

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' could describe a steak, tying it to food, but it is praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an exclamation praising an achievement and a description of what benefits your body.

clue.text: Remedying a deficiency that will make Underground announcement superfluous?

blocks.note: straight sense: making up a shortfall between two things

blocks.clueFragment: that will make Underground announcement superfluous
blocks.note: on the London Underground a recorded voice warns passengers to mind the space between train and platform; remove that space and the warning is unnecessary

explanation.surface: A fix so complete that the Tube no longer needs its famous warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Underground's recorded warning is 'Mind the gap'; CLOSING THE GAP would make it pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing the gap means eliminating a shortfall, such as between targets and results, which is remedying a deficiency.

clue.text: Heartless girl - an irritation, a difficulty

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letters are taken out, keeping only the ends

blocks.note: only the first and last letters remain
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: An unkind girlfriend who becomes a nuisance and a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: A glitch is a minor malfunction or hitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a small fault or hitch that causes trouble, so a minor difficulty.

clue.text: See 15
Town ultimately famous for having the glass

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
a lens is a shaped piece of glass

explanation.surface: A town renowned for its glassmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helens in Merseyside is genuinely famous for glass, home of the Pilkington glassworks, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helens is a town in Merseyside, north-west England, between Liverpool and Wigan.

clue.text: "A-Levels? I'd swot!" - possibly that's traditional "wisdom"

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A student vowing to study hard for exams, which may be just folk advice.
explanation.walkthrough: A-Levels are the English school-leaving exams taken at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wives' tales are popular superstitions and folk beliefs handed down, hence the ironic quotation marks around wisdom.

clue.text: See 19
Home for Ahab, one lamenting audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so we want a word that is spoken the same as this one

blocks.note: someone who wails in grief

explanation.surface: Captain Ahab's dwelling, and someone grieving out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Ahab in Moby-Dick commands the Pequod, a whaling ship, which is his home at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab lives aboard the Pequod, a ship hunting whales, so a whaling vessel is his home.

clue.text: Might they offer a drug to the man with an oral problem?

definitions.text: Might they offer a drug to the man with an oral problem?

blocks.note: taken as written
pot is slang for cannabis
the pronoun for a man
tooth decay, a problem in the mouth

explanation.surface: A question about who would dispense medicine to someone with toothache.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: old chemists would supply a remedy to a man with a bad tooth, and A + POT + HE + CARIES spells APOTHECARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Apothecaries were the old dispensing pharmacists who prepared and sold medicines to patients.

clue.text: Short programme for the handicapped?

blocks.note: surface reading: a brief scheme of help for people with disabilities
setter's reading: the clipped name of a recovery course for addicts and injured people

explanation.walkthrough: REHAB is short for rehabilitation, a programme to restore those disabled by injury or addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation courses help people regain abilities lost to illness, injury or dependency, and the clipped form is the word itself.

clue.text: Description of a decree to reverse one evil

indicators.note: to reverse is to turn backwards, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a sin is a wicked act

explanation.surface: A legal order to undo a wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A decree nisi is the provisional stage of an English divorce, made absolute later; ISIN read backwards gives NISI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisi, Latin for unless, qualifies a court decree that takes effect unless cause is shown otherwise.

clue.text: Trade in leather? The game's up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from bottom to top

blocks.note: first meaning: to sell, in informal British use
second meaning: to thrash or beat
the game of golf

explanation.surface: A dealer in leather goods discovers the con has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: to flog is British slang for sell, 'leather' is a verb meaning to beat, and in a down clue GOLF written upwards gives FLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to flog goods is to sell them, and to flog someone is to whip or thrash them.

clue.text: Poems that may come from silly bard leaving pub

indicators.note: the pub leaving the poet means those letters walk out of the word
the answer may come from the remaining letters once they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A foolish poet walks out of the pub, perhaps to write verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take BAR out of SILLY BARD to leave SILLYD, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idylls are short pastoral or descriptive poems, as in Tennyson's Idylls of the King.

clue.text: Presumably Mrs Marcos found this huge bird

blocks.clueFragment: Presumably Mrs Marcos found this huge
blocks.note: surface: Imelda Marcos, wife of the Philippine dictator, was notorious for owning thousands of pairs of footwear, so her account for them must have been enormous
setter's reading: a very large African stork named after its broad clog-shaped beak

explanation.surface: The famously footwear-loving Imelda Marcos facing an enormous invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SHOE BILL, it is the cost of footwear, which Imelda Marcos famously ran up; whole, it is a huge African wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoebill is a tall African stork-like wader standing over a metre high, so a very large bird.

clue.text: Assault on crossword grid carried out with military precision?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the activity so carried out

indicators.note: in an across entry, putting one thing on another places it after, so the assault comes second

blocks.note: a crossword grid is a square
a beating or attack

explanation.surface: An attack on a crossword grid, executed like a drill sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: Square-bashing is British slang for military drill on a parade ground; the assault goes on, that is after, the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Square-bashing is parade-ground drill, which soldiers perform in precise, regimented unison.

clue.text: See 28
